audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel chapter 18, first-pass draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for military organization, 'worth ten thousand' leader valuation, David's public protection order, twenty-thousand deaths, forest/terrain casualties, Absalom's entrapment, refusal of unlawful reward, Joab's execution and subordinates, dishonored burial, monument tradition, Cushite messenger identity, evasive reporting, and David's grief.

verses.restored: David mustered people with him and placed over them commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds.

familiar.text: And David numbered the people that were with him, and set captains of thousands and captains of hundreds over them.

verses.restored: David sent people: one third by hand of Joab, one third by hand of Abishai son of Zeruiah, brother of Joab, and one third by hand of Ittai the Gittite. King said to people, Going out, I will also go out with you.

familiar.text: And David sent forth a third part of the people under the hand of Joab, and a third part under the hand of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, Joab’s brother, and a third part under the hand of Ittai the Gittite. And the king said unto the people, I will surely go forth with you myself also.

verses.restored: People said, You shall not go out, because if we flee they will not set heart on us; if half of us die they will not set heart on us. Now you are like ten thousand of us. It is better now that you be for us from city to rescue/support.

familiar.text: But the people answered, Thou shalt not go forth: for if we flee away, they will not care for us; neither if half of us die, will they care for us: but now thou art worth ten thousand of us: therefore now it is better that thou succour us out of the city.

verses.restored: King said to them, What is good in your eyes I will do. King stood at side of gate, and all people went out by hundreds and thousands.

familiar.text: And the king said unto them, What seemeth you best I will do. And the king stood by the gate side, and all the people came out by hundreds and by thousands.

verses.restored: King commanded Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, saying, Gently for my sake with young man, with Absalom. All people heard when king commanded all commanders concerning Absalom.

familiar.text: And the king commanded Joab and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Deal gently for my sake with the young man, even with Absalom. And all the people heard when the king gave all the captains charge concerning Absalom.

verses.restored: People went out to field against Israel, and battle was in forest of Ephraim.

familiar.text: So the people went out into the field against Israel: and the battle was in the wood of Ephraim;

verses.restored: People of Israel were struck there before servants of David. Slaughter there was great on that day: twenty thousand.

familiar.text: Where the people of Israel were slain before the servants of David, and there was there a great slaughter that day of twenty thousand men.

verses.restored: Battle spread there over face of all land, and forest devoured more among people than sword devoured on that day.

familiar.text: For the battle was there scattered over the face of all the country: and the wood devoured more people that day than the sword devoured.

verses.restored: Absalom encountered servants of David. Absalom rode upon mule. Mule came under tangled branches of great tree, and his head was caught in tree. He was left between heavens and earth, while mule under him passed on.

familiar.text: And Absalom met the servants of David. And Absalom rode upon a mule, and the mule went under the thick boughs of a great oak, and his head caught hold of the oak, and he was taken up between the heaven and the earth; and the mule that was under him went away.

verses.restored: A man saw and told Joab, saying, Look, I saw Absalom hanging in tree.

familiar.text: And a certain man saw it, and told Joab, and said, Behold, I saw Absalom hanged in an oak.

verses.restored: Joab said to man who told him, Look, you saw—why did you not strike him there to ground? I would have given you ten silver pieces and a belt.

familiar.text: And Joab said unto the man that told him, And, behold, thou sawest him, and why didst thou not smite him there to the ground? and I would have given thee ten shekels of silver, and a girdle.

verses.restored: Man said to Joab, Even if I weighed upon my palms one thousand silver pieces, I would not stretch out my hand against son of king. In our ears king commanded you, Abishai, and Ittai, saying, Guard for me young man Absalom.

familiar.text: And the man said unto Joab, Though I should receive a thousand shekels of silver in mine hand, yet would I not put forth mine hand against the king’s son: for in our hearing the king charged thee and Abishai and Ittai, saying, Beware that none touch the young man Absalom.

verses.restored: Or I would have acted falsely against his life/my life, and no matter is hidden from king; you yourself would have stood apart against me.

familiar.text: Otherwise I should have wrought falsehood against mine own life: for there is no matter hid from the king, and thou thyself wouldest have set thyself against me.

verses.restored: Joab said, I will not wait thus before you. He took three staffs/darts in his hand and thrust them into heart/body of Absalom while he was still alive in heart of tree.

familiar.text: Then said Joab, I may not tarry thus with thee. And he took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he was yet alive in the midst of the oak.

verses.restored: Ten young men, bearers of Joab's armor, surrounded, struck Absalom, and put him to death.

familiar.text: And ten young men that bare Joab’s armour compassed about and smote Absalom, and slew him.

verses.restored: Joab blew shofar, and people returned from pursuing Israel, because Joab restrained people.

verses.restored: They took Absalom, threw him into a great pit in forest, and raised over him a very great heap of stones. All Israel fled, each to his tent.

familiar.text: And they took Absalom, and cast him into a great pit in the wood, and laid a very great heap of stones upon him: and all Israel fled every one to his tent.

verses.restored: Absalom in his lifetime had taken and raised for himself a pillar in valley of king, because he said, I have no son to cause my name to be remembered. He called pillar by his name, and it is called Monument of Absalom until this day.

familiar.text: Now Absalom in his lifetime had taken and reared up for himself a pillar, which is in the king’s dale: for he said, I have no son to keep my name in remembrance: and he called the pillar after his own name: and it is called unto this day, Absalom’s place.

verses.restored: Ahimaaz son of Zadok said, Please let me run and announce to king that YHWH judged/rescued him from hand of his enemies.

familiar.text: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, Let me now run, and bear the king tidings, how that the LORD hath avenged him of his enemies.

familiar.text: And Joab said unto him, Thou shalt not bear tidings this day, but thou shalt bear tidings another day: but this day thou shalt bear no tidings, because the king’s son is dead.

familiar.text: Then said Ahimaaz the son of Zadok yet again to Joab, But howsoever, let me, I pray thee, also run after Cushi. And Joab said, Wherefore wilt thou run, my son, seeing that thou hast no tidings ready?

verses.restored: Whatever may be, let me run. He said, Run. Ahimaaz ran by way of plain and passed Cushite.

familiar.text: But howsoever, said he, let me run. And he said unto him, Run. Then Ahimaaz ran by the way of the plain, and overran Cushi.

verses.restored: David sat between two gates. Watchman went to roof of gate by wall, lifted his eyes, saw, and look, a man running alone.

familiar.text: And David sat between the two gates: and the watchman went up to the roof over the gate unto the wall, and lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold a man running alone.

verses.restored: Watchman called and told king. King said, If alone, news is in his mouth. He came nearer and nearer.

familiar.text: And the watchman cried, and told the king. And the king said, If he be alone, there is tidings in his mouth. And he came apace, and drew near.

verses.restored: Watchman saw another man running. Watchman called to gatekeeper and said, Look, a man running alone. King said, This one also brings news.

familiar.text: And the watchman saw another man running: and the watchman called unto the porter, and said, Behold another man running alone. And the king said, He also bringeth tidings.

verses.restored: Watchman said, I see running of first like running of Ahimaaz son of Zadok. King said, He is a good man and comes with good news.

familiar.text: And the watchman said, Me thinketh the running of the foremost is like the running of Ahimaaz the son of Zadok. And the king said, He is a good man, and cometh with good tidings.

verses.restored: Ahimaaz called and said to king, Peace. He bowed to king with face to ground and said, Blessed be YHWH your Divine, who delivered men who lifted their hand against my lord king.

familiar.text: And Ahimaaz called, and said unto the king, All is well. And he fell down to the earth upon his face before the king, and said, Blessed be the LORD thy God, which hath delivered up the men that lifted up their hand against my lord the king.

verses.restored: King said, Is there peace for young man Absalom? Ahimaaz said, I saw a great tumult when Joab sent servant of king and your servant, but I do not know what.

familiar.text: And the king said, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Ahimaaz answered, When Joab sent the king’s servant, and me thy servant, I saw a great tumult, but I knew not what it was.

verses.restored: King said, Turn aside and stand here. He turned aside and stood.

familiar.text: And the king said unto him, Turn aside, and stand here. And he turned aside, and stood still.

verses.restored: Look, Cushite came. Cushite said, Let my lord king receive news, because YHWH judged/rescued you today from hand of all who rose against you.

familiar.text: And, behold, Cushi came; and Cushi said, Tidings, my lord the king: for the LORD hath avenged thee this day of all them that rose up against thee.

verses.restored: King said to Cushite, Is there peace for young man Absalom? Cushite said, May enemies of my lord king and all who rise against you for evil be like young man.

familiar.text: And the king said unto Cushi, Is the young man Absalom safe? And Cushi answered, The enemies of my lord the king, and all that rise against thee to do thee hurt, be as that young man is.

verses.restored: King trembled, went up to upper room over gate, and wept. Thus he said as he went: My son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom. Who would give that I had died in your place, Absalom, my son, my son.

familiar.text: And the king was much moved, and went up to the chamber over the gate, and wept: and as he went, thus he said, O my son Absalom, my son, my son Absalom! would God I had died for thee, O Absalom, my son, my son!

translation_notes: The claim that David is 'worth ten thousand' values the ruler over thousands of ordinary lives. Strategic importance does not establish greater human worth.
David's protection order is public and clear. Joab's killing of Absalom directly violates it.

The twenty thousand dead are participants in a civil war, not an anonymous obstacle to David's restoration. 'The forest devoured' may include terrain, pits, exposure, and chaotic flight rather than supernatural vegetation.
The Hebrew says Absalom's head was caught; it does not explicitly say his famous hair caused the entrapment. Moralizing vanity through hair is unwarranted.
The unnamed soldier refuses Joab's reward because he heard the king's order and anticipates Joab would abandon him. Refusal of an unlawful command is morally significant.
Joab wounds Absalom while suspended and ten armor-bearers complete the killing. This is execution of a trapped person, not fair combat.
Absalom's burial in a pit and stone heap degrades the defeated body. His monument and child tradition contain textual tension.
The Cushite messenger's ethnicity must not become a racial stereotype or servant caricature. He bears the truth Ahimaaz avoids.
David's lament is authentic parental grief, but wishing to die in Absalom's place is not a suicide model or proof he should have ignored the lives of his troops.
safety_note: Do not glorify civil-war casualties, rank a leader as more human than thousands, blame Absalom's hair, or praise Joab's insubordination. David's death-wish is grief language, not instruction. Center the refused unlawful order, the trapped young man, the messengers, the dead across both armies, and a father's devastating loss.
